title: Runtime choice matrix
summary: Choose the agent runtime by control, effort, protocol needs, isolation and where code must run: a Foundry prompt agent, a hosted agent, self-hosting on AKS or Container Apps with registration, or a Copilot Studio agent.
useIf: You must justify where an agent runs and what each option costs in control, operations and governance.
avoidIf: The runtime is already fixed by policy and you only need to wire identity or governance.

explain.md: The same agent can run in four homes. A **prompt agent** is config only and Foundry runs it with no code or compute to manage [[r1]]. A **hosted agent** is your code on per-session VM-isolated sandboxes with a dedicated Entra identity and endpoint [[r2]]. **Self-hosting on AKS or Container Apps** keeps code on infrastructure you run, and you register it for governance: Foundry Control Plane puts API Management in front as a proxy, and Agent 365 uses the SDK or registry sync [[r23]] [[r13]]. A **Copilot Studio** agent is built in a graphical, low-code studio and published to channels such as Teams, Microsoft Copilot, websites and mobile apps [[tr4]].

explain.title: Runtime decision tree
explain.alt: If code must run outside Foundry choose self-hosting with registration. If makers build it choose Copilot Studio. If developers build it and need custom code, protocols or files choose a hosted agent, otherwise a prompt agent.
explain.src:
flowchart TB
  Q1{Must code run outside Foundry?} -->|Yes| SH[Self-host on AKS or Container Apps, register it]
  Q1 -->|No| Q2{Who builds it?}
  Q2 -->|Makers, low-code| CS[Copilot Studio agent]
  Q2 -->|Developers| Q3{Custom code, protocols or files?}
  Q3 -->|Yes| HA[Hosted agent]
  Q3 -->|No| PA[Prompt agent]

explain.md: Each home trades the same four dials. **Control**: configuration only, your own code, total control, or low-code with harness choices. **Effort**: a prompt agent has nothing to run, a hosted agent has code but no cluster, and a self-hosted agent adds scaling, identity wiring, session persistence and patching (inference). **Protocols and isolation**: hosted agents offer Responses, Invocations, WebSocket, Activity and A2A inside per-session VM-isolated sandboxes, while self-hosting leaves both to you. **Governance**: Foundry identity and tracing for Foundry agents, registration for self-hosted ones, and the Agent 365 registry for Copilot Studio agents [[r16]].

explain.title: Pick a runtime
explain.prompt: Flip the three dials to see which runtime leads and why.

options.name: Self-host and register
options.summary: AKS or Container Apps plus registration.

config.why: Instructions, model and tools cover it [[r1]].

code.why: No place for custom runtime code.

devs.why: SDK or REST definitions fit CI/CD.

mine.why: It cannot run on your own hosts.

config.why: Container effort for a config-level need.

devs.why: Developers bring code and ship an image or .zip.

mine.why: It runs on Foundry-managed sandboxes, not your hosts.

code.why: Total control of code and protocols.

devs.why: Developers and platform engineers run it.

managed.why: You take on operations you could avoid.

mine.why: Code stays on your infrastructure and registration adds governance [[r23]].

config.why: Describe the agent, connect knowledge and tools [[tr4]].

code.why: Low-code studio with harness choices, not arbitrary code.

explain.takeaway: Start from where code may run and who builds it, then add control only as far as the requirement demands.

whereToUse: Architecture reviews that decide the runtime for a new agent
Migration plans moving agents between runtimes without losing governance
Interview answers that must defend a runtime with dials and flip conditions
Platform standards that set a default and name the exceptions

use: Default to the prompt agent for config-level needs, because it is the least to manage
Move to a hosted agent when you need your code, custom protocols or persistent files
Self-host when code must run on your infrastructure, then register it for governance
Choose Copilot Studio when makers own the agent and Microsoft 365 channels are the main surface
avoid: Hosting everything yourself by habit when a managed runtime meets the requirement
Choosing hosted agents on a policy that needs a documented GA label until you confirm status
Choosing by tool preference rather than by control, effort, protocols, isolation and governance
flips: A webhook or custom protocol requirement flips prompt agent to hosted agent
A residency or on-premises requirement flips hosted to self-hosted with registration
A maker team that owns the agent flips developer-built runtimes to Copilot Studio

pitfalls.symptom: Governance team cannot see an agent running on another cloud
pitfalls.cause: The agent was self-hosted and never registered
pitfalls.fix: Register it in Foundry Control Plane, use the Agent 365 SDK, or sync the registry [[r23]] [[r13]].

pitfalls.symptom: Cost and ops grow after moving to self-hosting 'for control'
pitfalls.cause: No requirement forced it, and you now run scaling, identity wiring and patching
pitfalls.fix: Revisit the decision tree and move back to a managed runtime unless residency or infrastructure rules demand it.

pitfalls.symptom: A Copilot Studio agent appears twice in the registry
pitfalls.cause: Separate publisher records for the same agent exist by design
pitfalls.fix: Use the publisher filter and check each record's actions [[r16]].

scenarios.title: Business team builds its own agent
scenarios.situation: A business team with no developers wants an agent for Teams that calls approved connectors and a knowledge source.
unknowns: Does it need custom code later?
scenarios.question: Which runtime do you pick?

options.name: Copilot Studio agent
options.why: A low-code studio for makers, published to Teams and Microsoft Copilot, and it appears in the Agent 365 registry.
options.tradeoff: Limited code control, and some features are preview.

options.name: Prompt agent in Foundry
options.why: No code and published to Teams.
options.tradeoff: Authoring is still engineer-oriented and uses a different governance surface.

options.name: Hosted agent
options.why: It needs developers, a container and compute for a need that low-code covers.
options.tradeoff: Right when custom code or protocols appear.

flips.if: The agent needs custom code or webhooks
flips.then: Hand it to developers on a hosted agent.

flips.if: Agents must live in Foundry for tracing and evals

scenarios.takeaway: Let the builder profile pick the home when control needs are modest.

scenarios.title: Code must stay in the data center
scenarios.situation: An existing agent runs in the company's own data center because of a residency rule. The governance team wants it visible and controlled alongside the cloud agents.
unknowns: Does it speak A2A or an OpenAI-compatible API?
Does it need governed Work IQ tools?
scenarios.question: What do you do?

options.name: Keep it on your infrastructure and register it (Control Plane, Agent 365 SDK or registry sync)
options.why: Code stays put, and registration gives inventory and access control.
options.tradeoff: You keep operating the runtime, and the capabilities differ by registration path.

options.name: Port it to a hosted agent with bring-your-own VNet
options.why: Managed sessions and identity while keeping network isolation.
options.tradeoff: The code and data path move into Azure, which the residency rule may forbid.

options.name: Rebuild it as a prompt agent
options.why: Loses the custom code and moves the workload off premises.
options.tradeoff: Right only for simple agents with no residency rule.

flips.then: Hosted agent becomes the lowest-ops path.
Registry sync with no code change.

scenarios.takeaway: Where code may run decides the home, and registration carries governance.

quiz.q: A residency rule says agent code must run in the company's data center, but central governance is required. What is the best fit?
quiz.explain: Self-hosting keeps code on your infrastructure, and registration (Control Plane, Agent 365 SDK or registry sync) gives governance. Hosted, prompt and Copilot Studio runtimes are Microsoft-managed.

quiz.q: Match each runtime to its defining trait.

pairs.r: Your code in per-session VM-isolated sandboxes

pairs.l: Self-hosted on AKS or Container Apps
pairs.r: Code on your infrastructure, registered for governance

quiz.explain: These follow the Foundry overview, the hosted agents page, the Control Plane registration page and the Copilot Studio overview.

quiz.q: Which are legitimate reasons to leave the prompt agent for a hosted agent?
options: You need persistent files across turns
You want fewer things to operate
You need to choose CPU and memory for sessions
quiz.explain: Webhooks, persistent files and compute control are the documented reasons. Wanting fewer things to operate points the other way, toward the prompt agent.

flashcards.front: Decision order for the runtime choice?
flashcards.back: First: must code run outside Foundry? Then: who builds it (makers or developers)? Then: custom code, protocols or files needed? Prompt agent unless a requirement forces more.

flashcards.front: How does a self-hosted agent get governance?
flashcards.back: Register it in Foundry Control Plane (API Management proxy), add the Agent 365 SDK, or use registry sync for connected platforms. You still host and run it.

flashcards.front: Which runtime lacks a documented GA label as of 2026-10-13?
flashcards.back: Hosted agents: no separate GA row and no explicit GA statement found (UNVERIFIED). Voice-based agents are preview.
